decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs), including ductility and toughness. Various processing techniques and alloy designs have been explored, such as selective laser melting, spark plasma sintering, and the addition of interstitial elements. The trend suggests that the introduction of specific elements or phases can enhance the mechanical properties of HEAs.
decision.unsolved: The improvement of ductility and toughness in HfZrTi HEAs remains a challenge. Current research has not fully addressed the optimization of this specific alloy system for enhanced ductility and toughness.
decision.lever: introduction of oxygen or nitrogen interstitials
decision.why: The introduction of interstitial elements, such as oxygen or nitrogen, has been shown to improve the mechanical properties of other HEA systems. This approach could be applied to the HfZrTi system to enhance its ductility and toughness, as seen in the case of the Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi base HEA with oxygen or nitrogen additions (record ID: PMC7299626).
